content: The tobacco industry in Argentina produced a total of 157,294 tonnes of tobacco during the 2003/2004 harvest season. Of this amount, the majority—93,327 tonnes—was exported. The total area dedicated to tobacco cultivation was 75 square kilometers, with 776 square kilometers being actively harvested. The industry is dominated by two major companies: Massalin Particulares (a subsidiary of Philip Morris International) and Nobleza Piccardo (a subsidiary of British American Tobacco). Nobleza Piccardo markets international brands such as Lucky Strike, Viceroy, and Camel, as well as local brands like Jockey and Derby. Tobacco production in Argentina is concentrated in the northern regions of the country. The provinces of Jujuy and Salta, located in the northwest, and Misiones, situated in the northeastern Mesopotamian region, are the leading producers, each contributing over 45,000 tonnes annually. Other provinces involved in tobacco production include Tucumán, Corrientes, Chaco, and Catamarca. Tobacco plays a significant role in the economies of these producing regions, which are among the poorer provinces in Argentina. The tobacco industry provides employment to approximately 500,000 people. About half of these workers are directly involved in planting and harvesting activities, while only around 2% are engaged in the manufacturing of tobacco-derived products. The remaining workforce is employed in distribution and sales. Despite the well-documented health consequences of smoking, which represent a major public health concern in Argentina, the national government supports tobacco producers through the Tobacco Special Fund (Fondo Especial del Tabaco, FET). This fund provides subsidies and facilitates access to credit, aiming to modernize the industry and sustain its economic viability.
